question.prompt: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(CA=CB.\) On \(CB\) square \(BCDE\) is constructed away from the triangle. If \(x\) is the number of degrees in angle \(DAB,\) then

solutions.explanation:
The useful observation is that the square supplies a third segment equal to the two given equal sides:
\[
CA=CB=CD.
\]
Therefore \(A,B,D\) lie on the circle with center \(C\) and radius \(CB\). The square also gives \(\angle BCD=90^\circ\).

Because the square is constructed away from the triangle, \(A\) and \(D\) lie on opposite sides of line \(BC\). The minor arc \(BD\) lies on the same side of this line as \(D\), so it does not contain \(A\). Thus \(\angle DAB\) is an inscribed angle intercepting that quarter-circle arc. An inscribed angle is half the central angle intercepting the same arc, giving
\[
x=\frac12\cdot90^\circ=45^\circ.
\]
This value is independent of the shape of triangle \(ABC\), so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Recognize a common circle

solutions.explanation:
Let \(\theta=\angle ACB\), where \(0^\circ<\theta<180^\circ\). Since \(CA=CB\), the base angles of triangle \(ABC\) give
\[
\angle CAB=\frac{180^\circ-\theta}{2}.
\]
Also, \(CA=CD\), so triangle \(ACD\) is isosceles whenever its three vertices are not collinear. The outward square puts ray \(CD\) perpendicular to \(CB\) on the side of line \(BC\) opposite \(A\). We consider the possible positions of ray \(CA\).

If \(0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ\), then \(\angle ACD=90^\circ+\theta\), so
\[
\angle CAD=\frac{90^\circ-\theta}{2}.
\]
In this position ray \(AD\) lies inside \(\angle CAB\). Therefore
\[
x=\angle CAB-\angle CAD=45^\circ.
\]
If \(90^\circ<\theta<180^\circ\), the smaller angle \(ACD\) is \(270^\circ-\theta\), so
\[
\angle CAD=\frac{\theta-90^\circ}{2}.
\]
Here ray \(AC\) lies between rays \(AD\) and \(AB\). Hence
\[
x=\angle CAD+\angle CAB=45^\circ.
\]
Finally, if \(\theta=90^\circ\), then \(A,C,D\) are collinear, with \(C\) between \(A\) and \(D\). Rays \(AC\) and \(AD\) coincide, so \(x=\angle CAB=45^\circ\).

Every nondegenerate triangle is covered, and \(x\) is always \(45^\circ\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Use isosceles triangles
